title: Reading a Middle Kingdom Stela
short: A stela starts with the offering formula, names the gods, lists the gifts, then names the owner and his titles.
trouble: Students read top to bottom without checking direction. Find which way the signs face before you start.

blocks.html: A Middle Kingdom stela is a slab of stone, usually round-topped, set up in a tomb chapel or at a holy place like Abydos. Thousands survive, and most follow one plan. You already know its opening from The Offering Formula and its list of gifts from Bread, Beer and the Voice Offering. Now read it as a whole.

A stela's text usually runs: (1) the formula ḥtp-dj-nsw "an offering that the king gives"; (2) the god or gods, with their titles; (3) the gifts, dj=f prt-ḫrw t ḥnqt kꜣ ꜣpd… "that he may give an invocation offering of bread and beer, oxen and fowl…"; (4) n kꜣ n "for the ka of" the owner, with his titles and name, often ending mꜣꜥ-ḫrw "true of voice".

The stela is a request that never expires. The king, in theory the only one who could make offerings to the gods, gives an offering; the god passes its benefit on to the dead; and anyone who reads the text aloud makes the "invocation offering" (prt-ḫrw, literally "going out of the voice") real again. That is why the gifts are listed so carefully, and why the owner's name must be there: the offering is for that ka and no other.

opts.en: an offering that the king gives (to) Osiris

blocks.cap: Written right to left, as on many stelae: the signs face right, toward the start of the line.

head: Part
Typical words
Meaning
rows: an offering that the king gives
wsjr nb ḏdw nṯr ꜥꜣ nb ꜣbḏw
Osiris, lord of Busiris, the great god, lord of Abydos
Anubis, who is upon his mountain, lord of the sacred land
dj=f prt-ḫrw t ḥnqt kꜣ ꜣpd šs mnḫt ḫt nbt nfrt wꜥbt
that he may give an invocation offering of bread and beer, oxen and fowl, alabaster and linen, every good and pure thing
n kꜣ n jmꜣḫy NN mꜣꜥ-ḫrw
for the ka of the revered one NN, true of voice

blocks.title: The gift line
steps: dj=f: the sḏm=f of rdj, a wish after the god's name (What the sḏm=f Means).
blocks.a: "That he may give an invocation offering of bread and beer."

blocks.title: The owner
steps: n "for", kꜣ "the ka", then the genitive n "of".
jmꜣḫy "the revered one", a common title of the honored dead.
blocks.a: "For the ka of the revered one."

blocks.html: Below or beside the text there is often a picture of the owner seated before a table of offerings, sometimes with his family (Families on Stelae). The words and the picture belong together: the bread and beer named in the text are the ones heaped on the table.

Reading top to bottom, or left to right, without checking the direction. Stela texts run in rows or columns, and very often right to left. Check before you start: find a sign with a face (a bird, a person, the horned viper) and see which way it looks. It faces the beginning of the line.
